clue.text: Delivery man at the door

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a short ball that rears up at the batsman
a doorman who keeps unwanted guests out of a club

explanation.surface: A courier waiting on the doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a short-pitched cricket ball, and a nightclub's doorman who throws out troublemakers.

clue.text: Flaming, as red

definitions.meaning: a mild British swear word, as in 'flaming nuisance'

explanation.surface: Something burning and glowing crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a British expletive intensifier like 'flaming', and the colour of blood.

clue.text: Headless cockroach, say, with a place in Africa

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter of the insect word is dropped

parts.note: a cockroach is an example of a bug
with means and

explanation.surface: A decapitated insect found somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' removes B from BUG, leaving UG.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked East African country, a place on that continent.

clue.text: Fare traditionally served as ticket held in kind of poetic justice, ultimately

indicators.note: held in means the ticket word sits inside the rearranged letters
kind of signals a variant form of the word poetic, its letters shuffled

parts.note: a tag is a label or ticket

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of justice

explanation.surface: Poetic justice as a ticket being dished out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' makes an anagram of the clue word, opened by 'held in' around the label; 'ultimately' takes only the last letter of 'justice'. 'Fare' means food here, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British dish of minced meat topped with mashed potato, served as food.

clue.text: Something to restore, because it's an old instrument

indicators.note: something to the words means a part of them, the letters concealed inside

explanation.surface: An antique instrument that needs restoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'restore' and the start of 'because'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval bowed stringed instrument, an early ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: Demonic spirit in political opponents, one detailed

indicators.note: one of the pair loses its tail, so the last letter of the first country goes

parts.note: Cuba and the US are long-time political foes
the United States, Cuba's long-time political foe

explanation.surface: A devil lurking among one's political rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The political opponents are the Caribbean island nation and its big northern neighbour; 'one detailed' means only the first of the pair loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A male demon of folklore said to lie upon sleepers, an evil supernatural being.

clue.text: Performing as one

explanation.surface: Acting together on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both playing live on stage and acting jointly in agreement.

clue.text: See 19
Rocky, as in sea

indicators.note: in means the small word goes inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe

explanation.surface: Choppy conditions at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of basalt, a dark volcanic stone, so consisting of rock.

clue.text: Wise to buttonhole crew for long-gone train times

indicators.note: to buttonhole is to grab someone, here the wise word holds the crew word inside it

parts.note: sage means wise
a team is a crew

explanation.surface: A wise person collaring a train crew about old timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical era when railways ran on locomotives powered by boiling water, now passed.

clue.text: Old component for modern works

parts.note: a part is a component

explanation.surface: Swapping an antique part into something contemporary.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical art, a 1960s style of painting built on visual illusions, so a body of modern pictures.

clue.text: Second question for old newspaper

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
an issue is a question under discussion

explanation.surface: Asking a follow-up question about an old paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A previously published copy of a periodical, no longer the current edition.

clue.text: Add an embarrassing mid-life performance?

parts.note: the word Add is what results when the letters of a father's pet name are jumbled up, as if jigging about

explanation.surface: An instruction to include an awkward middle-aged display.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'dancing' acts on DAD, rearranging it to ADD, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The awkward jigging of middle-aged fathers at parties, a cringeworthy show.

clue.text: Fifty boards to stick down

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so the Roman numeral climbs inside the sticking word

parts.note: to gum is to stick
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty planks to be glued down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being miserable or dejected, a matching mood adjective.

clue.text: Letters in an anagram are so not working!

definitions.text: Letters in an anagram are so
definitions.meaning: an anagram's letters are jumbled out of their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A grumble that a jumbled word puzzle is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both muddled in sequence and broken, like a faulty machine.

clue.text: Putting off green, child has us beaten

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are, so the letters are whisked into a new order

explanation.surface: A child beating us on the golf green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' mixes the letters of GREEN, CHILD and US together; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponing means moving an event to a later date, which is delaying it.

clue.text: Needlewoman sees Manx cat biting Manx cat biting cat's tail

indicators.note: biting means the first cut-short cat holds the rest in its mouth
a Manx cat has no tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

indicators.note: biting again means the second shortened cat encloses one more letter
tailless again, so the spotted big cat loses its final letter

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of the word cat

explanation.surface: A seamstress watching tailless cats nibbling at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man, so 'Manx' clips the last letter of each cat; the second cat is a big one, the spotted kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen gave her name to the obelisk in London called her Needle, so she is jokingly a woman with a needle.

clue.text: Quiet thus, vacuum won't start

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: won't start means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a vacuum contains nothing

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner that is silent because it will not switch on.
explanation.definitionFit: Calming and gentle, as quiet music is restful; an adjective for something that soothes.

clue.text: Eating heartily, scoff as setter, perhaps?

indicators.note: eating means the mocking word takes in the other word

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff
well means heartily, as in eating well

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter wolfing down food and sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the crossword compiler; here it is someone who sets gems in rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who sets precious stones into mounts is one kind of stone setter.

clue.text: A pop sensation, no two ways about it!

definitions.meaning: a hugely successful British-Irish boy band
a single way, only the one route

explanation.surface: A pop star whose fame is beyond doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a chart-topping boy band, and literally a single way rather than two.

clue.text: Facial feature two inches out?

parts.note: a fold of fat beneath the jaw makes the lower face jut out, as if two jaws stacked

explanation.surface: A face feature protruding a couple of inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in two lights; the facial feature is twice what it should be, sticking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold of fatty flesh below the jaw line, a feature of the lower face.

clue.text: Probing of Milibands by computers, censored

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the computer word goes inside the pair of names

parts.note: Ed Miliband, former Labour leader; two of him give two Eds
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: Computers prying into the Miliband brothers, with results suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband is a British Labour politician, brother of David; the plural is taken cheekily as two of Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and revised, as a censor prunes material before release.

clue.text: One joining the bank

definitions.meaning: a row or level, such as a bank of seats

explanation.surface: A new member signing up at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person who ties knots and a row in a stepped series, like a bank.

clue.text: Where atheists might look to steal love, as mischievous

indicators.note: to steal means to slip in quietly, so the zero letter creeps inside the phrase

parts.note: atheists looking heavenward see no god, so they look up to no god
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Godless people searching for love and getting into mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engaged in mischief or plotting something naughty is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Confess that was painful joke (not written down)

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

indicators.note: in a down clue, not written down means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: Admitting that a joke was dreadful and best not recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not written down' reverses PUN to NUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit to something, such as a misdeed, is the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: Sweet ass

definitions.meaning: a dessert of stewed fruit and cream

explanation.surface: An endearing donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a creamy fruit pudding and a silly person.

clue.text: Crooked letters in long title misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters are put in the wrong places, mixed up

explanation.surface: A long title spelt with its letters jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained by dishonest means, like crooked gains or stolen goods.

clue.text: Start due, no middle though

indicators.note: no middle means the central letter of due is dropped, keeping its ends

parts.note: but means though

explanation.surface: Something about to begin, though not halfway yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A first appearance or launch, the beginning of a career.

clue.text: Beast who's thuggish or evil in silverback?

indicators.note: in means the two words sit inside the reversed silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is silver's chemical symbol; back reverses it
ill means evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Is the silverback ape a brute or evil?
explanation.walkthrough: 'silverback' splits as 'silver back', the chemical symbol for silver turned round; a silverback is also a mature male of the very beast defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape, and slang for a burly heavy or thug.

clue.text: Left back, mean

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the end is the back

explanation.surface: Something left behind with nasty intent.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or signify is to mean, as clouds mean rain.
